consensus_summary: Consensus primaries converge on total irreversible destruction, judgment, or removal: the sea is the place of no return, applied especially to millstone/Babylon judgment texts, with common secondary readings for faith removing mountains/trees and for sins cast away.
book_summary: A ruling power irreversibly destroyed and sunk into the sea of peoples, never to rise; especially the fall of Babylon the Great.
consensus_core_identification: irreversible destruction/judgment/removal of an entity into the sea as place of no return
book_core_identification: irreversible destruction of a ruling power sunk into the sea of peoples (esp. Babylon)
boundary_disagreement: Book limits the symbol to ruling powers (Babylon foremost) entering the sea of peoples; consensus admits broader cases including personal faith-obstacles, sins forgiven, general wicked persons, and non-political objects, while treating sea-as-nations as only one minority frame.
rationale: Both cores share the irreversible-sinking/final-overthrow motif anchored in Rev 18:21, Jer 51:63-64 and Exodus drowning imagery. The book keeps that category intact but narrows the subject from any judged/removed entity to ruling powers and re-specifies the sea as peoples—an identification already present among consensus alternatives—yielding a refined rather than replaced referent. Faith-mountain/tree and ship citations are retained yet subordinated to the narrowed political reading.
strongest_objection: Printed references include Matt 21:21 and Luke 17:6, which consensus uniformly reads as faith-hyperbole rather than overthrow of a ruling power, so the book's single definition appears to reclassify those cases without textual warrant in the entry itself.
